howTo.title: From your numbers to a media buying plan
howTo.intro: Most plans take five to ten minutes. Here is what each step and tab asks for, and where to find the numbers.
howTo.tabsIntro: You only see the tabs that apply to your business type and account.

tabs.setup: Pick your niche, regions, planning month and currency, then your target clients or sales, or your fixed monthly budget.
tabs.business: For lead generation: client value, margin and your booking, show-up and close rates. For ecommerce: order value, product cost, shipping, fees and returns.
tabs.account: Only for accounts with data: spend, impressions, reach, clicks and results per country, plus Google Search numbers. You can import a CSV export.
tabs.estimates: Only for new accounts: CPM, CTR and conversion rates for Meta, and search volume, bids and rates for Google, each with a source label.
tabs.planning: How many Meta ad sets and creatives you plan to run, the test length and whether to include retargeting.
tabs.advanced: Learning thresholds, buffers, range multipliers and seasonality. Defaults are filled in, so most people never change them.

howTo.whereIntro: Use the same date range in every platform. 30 days is a good default.

meta.title: About
meta.description: What the planner does, how it calculates budgets in plain language, and why every result is an estimate.

about.title: About {brand}
about.intro: {brand} turns your business numbers into an ad budget and a media buying plan for Meta and Google Search.

sections.heading: What it does
body: It answers the questions every media buyer asks before spending: how much budget do we need, what will it deliver, can we afford it, and how should it be split across platforms?
It works for lead generation and ecommerce, for new accounts and accounts with history, and in seven languages.

sections.heading: How it works, in plain language
body: Your business numbers set the limits. Client value and margin, or order value and costs, decide the most you can pay for a client, a lead or a sale.
Data or tests find the real cost. With account history we start from what results actually cost you. Without it, we plan a test budget and clear rules for what to do once real costs come in.
Then we account for how costs rise as you scale, the learning phase on each platform, and how much Google Search can actually deliver.

sections.heading: Results are estimates
body: Every plan is an estimate, not a promise. Ad costs change with your creatives, offer, competition, season and platform updates. Use the plan to decide what to test and how much to risk, then update it with real results.

sections.heading: Your data stays with you
body: Planner inputs are saved in your browser only. Nothing you enter in the planner is sent to our servers.
